user_message: Why does an accelerating electric charge radiate in the standard inertial-observer setting, while a charge moving uniformly in an inertial frame does not? Mention one caveat about how radiation is identified.
allowed_evidence: For a localized charge in classical electrodynamics, the far-zone field seen by asymptotic inertial observers contains an acceleration-dependent term that falls as 1/r; its energy flux integrated over a large sphere can remain finite. Uniform inertial motion has no such radiation term. Accelerated observers, curved spacetime, and non-asymptotic settings can complicate how radiation is identified.
public_rubric: Distinguishes near or velocity fields from far-zone radiation.
Connects radiation to the acceleration-dependent 1/r field and its energy flux.
Acknowledges an observer, boundary, or spacetime caveat without obscuring the standard case.
